move.speaker: Phil Halper
move.proposition: Current early-universe models warrant agnosticism until they produce precise predictions that survive thorough observational testing.
move.sourceExcerpt: I don't believe any of the models in our book, right? And the reason is because I won't believe it until we've made really precise predictions that have been tested thoroughly against observations. components.text: Whether speculative early-universe alternatives should be judged established before they yield precise, thoroughly tested observational predictions.
Whether alleged theoretical inputs justify rejecting models before their distinctive predictions receive observational tests.
Whether current evidence is sufficiently discriminating to warrant more than agnosticism among global histories.

response.rationale: Halper replaces premature model acceptance or rejection with a prediction-and-testing standard and justifies it by present model simplification and non-compulsion.

move.speaker: Stephen Meyer
move.proposition: Life-permitting cosmic parameters occupy exceptionally narrow ranges, and ordinary causal experience associates comparably constrained systems with minds, supporting an inference to designing intelligence.
